title: acceptance.sh AT03 captured stderr that nothing ever read, so a noisy success looked silent
body:
`acceptance.sh` AT03 captured the build's stderr to `$WORK/at03.err` and nothing
ever read the file. The redirect was there to keep the terminal tidy, so A BUILD
THAT SUCCEEDED NOISILY WAS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A SILENT ONE.

The consequence is not hypothetical. AT03 builds `examples/demo.md`, which until
issue 0012 applied a slide class no theme declares. prez warned on that build
EVERY TIME THE SUITE RAN, the harness wrote 165 bytes into `at03.err` on each
run, and the suite reported 14/0/0/0 green throughout. hv found the warning by
eye, in a terminal, running the render loop by hand -- discovering what this
file had been recording all along.

POPULATION, measured rather than estimated, because the first two attempts at
this count were both wrong and landed one apart:

    all 2> sites   78
      2>&1 merges  44   (visible: stderr joins stdout)
      2>/dev/null  18   (deliberate discards)
      literal .err 13   (8 under $WORK, 5 AT13 legs under $AT13DIR)
      via a var     3   ($err, $at15out, $at15nobin)
      accounted    78   remainder 0

Of the 16 `.err` captures, FIFTEEN ARE READ by a `present`/`absent` assertion.
`at03.err` was the only write-only one. The suite's discipline was good; this
was a genuine one-off and not a policy problem, and it is fixed as one.

FIX: `check "the build says nothing on stderr" ... "0"` in AT03, asserting the
capture is zero bytes rather than asserting a particular needle is absent -- a
needle-based check only catches the noise you already thought of.

PROVEN RED-FIRST, which is the whole point and was nearly skipped. Adding the
assertion after 0012 had already landed would have parked a green in a frozen
suite that had never been observed to fail (`IN-AG-RED-CONTROL-001`). So the
class line was re-injected into demo.md and the suite run against it:

    defect present   FAIL the build says nothing on stderr = 165, wanted 0
                     exit 1, passed 13 failed 1
    defect absent    ok   the build says nothing on stderr = 0
                     exit 0, passed 14 failed 0

demo.md is byte-identical to HEAD afterwards; the injection left no trace.

The first injection attempt SILENTLY DID NOT APPLY -- the anchor
`<!-- background: #101418 -->` occurs twice in demo.md, once inside a fenced
directives example at line 54 and once live at line 62 -- and the suite was run
anyway, returning a green that meant nothing. The rewrite's own `count == 1`
assertion caught it. A gate now refuses to run the red proof unless the defect
is confirmed present, because a red proof against an unmodified file is not a
proof of anything.

ALSO REMOVED: `theme-addressing.sh:224`, `cp "$WORK/refuses.err"
"$D/dir-refusal.err"`. The copy was never read. No false green -- the
assertion above it runs first -- so this is dead weight rather than a defect.
